absent: Santos is not cited despite 'inter-knowledge'; the concept is developed from Mexican sources (Bonfil, Zemelman) instead. Little English-language TD literature.
forYou: Greenwood & Levin (2007) is here: if your 'Levin' is Morten Levin, this paper puts him in dialogue with Fals Borda. Stavenhagen (1971) is an early, rarely cited source for your decolonial line.
method: References from Crossref; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in the reference list and title.
narrative: This paper stands in the Latin American founding line of PAR: Stavenhagen's 'Decolonializing applied social sciences' (1971) and Fals Borda's 'Ciencia propia y colonialismo intelectual' (1976) and 'El problema de cómo investigar la realidad para transformarla' (1979).

Its second root is the author's own history: five decades of work in San Miguel Tzinacapan, from the 1980s participatory research centre to recent writing on Zapatismo. Community-authored texts are cited as sources, not as data.
Northern action research appears mainly as Greenwood and Levin's 'Introduction to action research' (2007), which the paper sets against a lived, solidarity-based practice.
